messages:
maria: nightly-bot flagged a pretty big regression from last night's eval on summ-v2 for rwd/llama3-13b-int8-calib. ROUGE-L dropped ~7 pts vs fp16 baseline. can we triage?

nightly-bot: Report: run=nightly-run-20260317-03, model=rwd/llama3-13b-int8-calib, testset=summ-v2, rouge_l=0.412 (fp16 baseline 0.484), kl_logit=0.232, failures=173/200 :warning:

kai: ugh. can you dump one or two example diffs (gt / fp16 / int8)?

maria: here's a quick example from the run:
```
GT: The committee recommended delaying the rollout until further testing.
FP16: The committee recommended delaying the rollout until further testing and review.
INT8: The committee recommended delaying the rollout until further
```
INT8 usually truncates mid-sentence or repeats tokens, sometimes collapses to short fragments.

tj: did we change the calibration set or quant defaults recently?

maria: calib file used: calib_v3.jsonl (deployed 2 days ago). sample size ~5k. previous nightly used calib_v2 (~50k) iirc.

olga: that was my change — I swapped to a smaller focused sample to speed CI (PR #842). didn't expect this magnitude.

ryan: another angle: any runtime kernel changes? kernel-level fused ops can alter activation distributions visible to the quantizer.

kai: i did flip a default in the quantizer config last week (commit abc1234) toggling per_channel_quant -> false (we moved to per-tensor by default).

maria: repro command i used locally:
```bash
./tools/run_eval.sh --model rwd/llama3-13b \ 
  --quant int8 --calib calib_v3.jsonl 
  --prompts summ-v2 --seed 42 --out out_int8.json
```
float16 baseline command same minus --quant, reproduces expected rouge ~0.48. int8 reproduces the drop.

maria: i also dumped layer activation summaries — notable attenuation around layer 7 pre-activation:
```
layer, fp16_mean, int8_mean
6, 0.182, 0.049
7, 0.173, 0.041  <-- big drop
8, 0.167, 0.160
```
suggests a scale mismatch or per-channel scaling issue for specific channels in that layer.

tj: could be per-tensor scaling collapsing one channel's dynamic range. try per-channel quant and re-run quickly.

kai: running that now with per_channel_quant=true and per_channel_zero_point=true.

kai: quick results: with per-channel enabled rouge_l=0.472, kl_logit=0.048. almost back to baseline. :tada:

maria: nice. so root cause looks like the config switch + smaller calib sample exposed a fragility where per-tensor scales miss some channel peaks.

ryan: action items: revert default to per-channel, increase calib sample to at least 25k, and add a unit/regtest that checks summary stats vs fp16 for summ-v2. open an issue.

olga: i'll prepare a PR to revert the default and bump calib sample. also will add a note to docs about safe defaults.

maria: i'll open a folio with a small reproducer (3 prompts) and attach layer stats + sample outputs to the ticket.

nightly-bot: created issue #1543: "INT8 calibration/scale regression exposed by per-tensor default + small calib sample (summ-v2)" https://go/repo/issue/1543

tj: additional suggestion: log per-layer channel scales during calibration and fail nightly if any channel scale < 0.02 relative to fp16 mean for that layer. would detect this earlier.

kai: agreed — adding layerwise-scale logging is cheap. i'll put a quick patch up.

olga: ack, i'll include the calib_v2->v3 diff in the issue so we can track the dataset change.

ryan: schedule a short sync if we need a canary rollback later today — otherwise PRs as discussed. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — triage good. i'll paste the reproducer link in #incidents if things regress in the next nights.

kai: small followup: commit abc1234 is the change; i'll reference it in the PR to revert.

olga: will also add an eval case that runs int8 with per-tensor vs per-channel and asserts <= 1.5 pt rouge_l gap.

maria: marking this thread resolved for now, will update issue #1543 with attachments and next steps. :white_check_mark:
